children: Mexico's headline inflation likely accelerated in the first half of October while core inflation stabilized, a Reuters survey showed on Tuesday, supporting expectations the central bank will keep its key interest rate on hold for an extended period.

The median of 15 estimates showed general headline inflation at 3.60% year-on-year, up from 3.49% in the second half of September. If confirmed, it would mark the third consecutive half-month increase.
Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, is expected to hold at 3.70% annually, unchanged from the previous reading after four consecutive declines.

On a half-monthly basis, the National Consumer Price Index was expected to rise 0.37%, with local bank Banamex attributing the increase mainly to seasonal pressures on electricity tariffs and higher tourism service prices.
The core component was expected to increase 0.18% in the first-half of the month, the poll showed.

In September, the central bank held its benchmark rate at 6.50% and said it would not automatically follow in the steps of the US Federal Reserve, which raised interest rates last month for the first time since 2023.
Minutes from the Bank of Mexico's meeting showed three of five board members would be open to future rate cuts if inflation prospects improve.
Mexico's national statistics institute INEGI will release the inflation figures on Thursday.
